term.def: The servers, chips and networks that run AI tools behind the scenes. When companies plan for AI growth, this is usually what needs upgrading first.

prompt.prompt: List three tasks in [team or department] where letting an AI tool act on its own, without a human checking first, could go wrong. Suggest a safeguard for each.

quiz.q: TechCrunch reports Yale's Sonnenfeld called Nvidia a 'detriment' to US industrial might, not a champion.
quiz.why: This directly reflects what TechCrunch reported about his comments.

quiz.q: Reuters reports Dell raised its annual forecasts after a record quarter driven by surging AI server demand.
quiz.why: This matches what Reuters reported about Dell's results.

quiz.q: AI systems understand meaning the same way humans do.
quiz.why: AI finds patterns in data and predicts likely answers. It does not understand ideas the way a person does.

quiz.q: Feeding an AI model more data automatically makes its answers more accurate.
quiz.why: Quality and relevance of data matter more than sheer volume. Bad or messy data can make results worse.

quiz.q: AI tools can sound confident while still giving a wrong answer.
quiz.why: This is a well known limitation called hallucination, so checking important outputs is still necessary.
